scope: Exactly 12 active Phase 3 census study IDs, including newly source-confirmed post-readout FUSION, FDA supporting zilganersen study, and peer-reviewed OASISplus extension.
warnings: No new numerical clinical grade or RAAS FDA approval probability is created from source facts.
Open-label extensions are not interchangeable with the parent randomized pivotal studies.
Registry-derived source dates are the historical updates indicated by the linked source, not continuous live monitoring.
Three older Pre-Data labels are corrected by exact-trial issuer, FDA or peer-reviewed evidence; active count stays 258.

facts.evidence: FUSION efficacy primary outcome is a joint-rank functional/ventilation-free survival assessment through study Day 505; this is endpoint definition only, not evidence of achieving it.

Multicenter FUSION has a 60-week randomized placebo-controlled Part 1 (ION363 versus placebo, 2:1), then open-label extension phases. Registered Phase 1-3 is a mixed phase; do not infer Phase 3-only design.
89 patients reported enrolled (actual), as of July 2026 registry-derived update; sample size does not establish statistical power.
FDA states NCT04849741 included 49 randomized controlled patients aged 2 years or older plus four patients under age 2 in an open-label substudy; 53 patients in these components, not 54.
Open-label eplontersen long-term study records change from baseline in platelet count as an outcome. It is not the pivotal trial's clinical efficacy verdict.
This is a long-term open-label study of eplontersen; no placebo comparison is established for this extension, so comparator adequacy cannot be presumed.
151 patients are listed in the source's dated registry summary; this describes the long-term follow-up cohort, not a confirmatory efficacy-power calculation.
Phase 3 open-label extension of BALANCE (NCT04568434) in FCS; parent-trial efficacy must not be assigned to this extension.
Up to 60 participants planned for the FCS olezarsen open-label extension. This is a planned cohort size.
Phase 3 multicenter open-label safety study in patients with FCS previously treated with volanesorsen; 209-week olezarsen treatment period.
24 patients in the registered long-term open-label safety study; not a randomized pivotal efficacy cohort.

Published Year-1 OASISplus OLE cohort (83 participants): 22 patients (27%) reported treatment-related adverse events, none classified as serious treatment-related events; safety data are descriptive and do not establish a comparative clinical grade.
The published one-year OASISplus open-label extension subset included 83 participants (69 on Q4W and 14 on Q8W). This is the reported OLE subset, not total NCT05392114 enrollment.

Published open-label OASISplus Year-1 reduction in mean hereditary-angioedema attack rate compared with baseline: 94% Q4W and 95% Q8W. This is an uncontrolled within-cohort observation, not a placebo-adjusted efficacy PASS.
Published one-year OASISplus extension subgroup completion: 75 of 83 participants (90.4%). Do not infer the entire extension study has completed.

Published peer-reviewed exact-NCT OASISplus one-year open-label extension cohort report dated Feb 23, 2026: 83 patients; primary safety described with 22/83 reporting treatment-related adverse events, no related serious AEs. Nonbinary endpoint interpretation.
Long-term eplontersen ATTR-CM extension primarily evaluates safety and tolerability over extended dosing; not a new randomized efficacy superiority study.
Multicenter open-label Phase 3 extension from ION-682884-CS2, up to 36 months of eplontersen dosing; parent pivotal results must remain separate.
Approximately 1,400 participants planned for eplontersen ATTR-CM long-term extension. Enrollment target is not a completed enrollment or statistical power claim.

CORE-OLE primary follow-up evaluates clinical laboratory changes, adverse events and concomitant medication use through Week 157. This is an extension safety assessment, not proof of clinical benefit.
Open-label extension after SHTG CORE/CORE2 parent trials, with 157-week treatment and 13-week follow-up. Parent trial outcomes may not be duplicated as extension outcomes.
Approximately 885 patients participating in the dated institution listing; source describes extension enrollment rather than a placebo-controlled efficacy sample.
Issuer identifies Bayley-4 expressive communication as primary endpoint of pivotal REVEAL cohort; planned readout anticipated 2H 2027, no prospective success inferred.
Global Phase 3 REVEAL is randomized, double blind and controlled, with pediatric pivotal cohort and separate adult cohort. Do not treat the pooled cohorts as one endpoint sample.
Issuer reported 136 participants enrolled in pivotal pediatric cohort as of July 6, 2026; approximately 158 targeted overall. Enrollment is not trial outcome.
Issuer lists secondary endpoints including disease severity, cognition, sleep, motor function and daily-living skills. Endpoint existence is not an efficacy result.

Pediatric donidalorsen trial has safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics as objectives, including treatment-emergent adverse events as a primary measure; not a placebo-controlled pivotal efficacy outcome.
Registered pediatric HAE study is nonrandomized and open label with three weight-based dose groups; this cannot be scored as an RCT.
Target enrollment 20 pediatric patients aged 2 through 11 years; estimated, not actual accrual.
Pediatric FCS olezarsen study evaluates fasting triglyceride change as an efficacy outcome, with prospective longitudinal safety/PK/PD. No results yet adjudicated.
Phase 3 pediatric FCS trial is open label and multicenter, with one-year treatment and optional long-term extension; no placebo comparison is claimed.
12 participants expected across the pediatric FCS study; estimated recruitment target, not study completion.
CHAMPION Cohort 1 primary endpoint is Bayley-4 expressive communication raw score change without caregiver input at Week 52; endpoint definition, not outcome.
CHAMPION is a single-group open-label Phase 3 study in UPD/imprinting-defect Angelman syndrome, not the placebo-controlled REVEAL cohort.
Target enrollment 30 participants for CHAMPION (anticipated), with the registry reporting September 2026 study start.
Ionis reports most ulefnersen FUSION adverse events were mild or moderate. Sponsor topline safety statement is descriptive and not an independent safety grade.

Issuer reports statistically significant secondary endpoints including serum neurofilament light chain change and time to death/permanent ventilation/rescue or progression-related withdrawal; trial-level results, not an FDA decision.

Exact FUSION (ION363 / ulefnersen) Phase 3 topline issuer readout dated Sept 22, 2026: prespecified primary functional/survival joint-rank test reported positive, p=0.0005. Observed outcome not a prospective forecast.

FDA identifies the supporting NCT04849741 pivotal main study as a 49-patient multicenter randomized controlled comparison and a separate four-patient open-label pediatric substudy; do not merge the design arms.

FDA explicitly identifies NCT04849741 as an efficacy-and-safety supporting clinical study of approved zilganersen (ZANVASTRO). This is approval evidence, not a separately adjudicated binary trial primary endpoint.

FDA approved ZANVASTRO (zilganersen) for Alexander disease on Sept 3, 2026; application-level historical approval explicitly crosswalked to study NCT04849741. FDA outcome is NOT a numeric RAAS probability.
OASISplus one-year open-label extension patients reported mean AE-QoL improvement at Week 52: 28.1 points Q4W, 26.7 points Q8W; uncontrolled comparison, not placebo adjusted.
